newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila extends 3 percent cement tariff until 1998.
newsitem.headline: Manila extends 3 percent cement tariff until 1998.

text.p: The Philippines has postponed the introduction of a 10 percent tariff on imported portland cement until the end of 1998 because of a projected shortage in cement supply, the National Economic Development Authoritiy (NEDA) said on Thursday.
The current 3.0 percent tariff will remain in force until then. It was to have been replaced by the 10 percent duty on January 1 next year, the NEDA said.
Citing a Department of Trade and Industry study, NEDA said the cement shortage will persist until 1998. Demand is projected to increase by an average of 20 percent yearly.
This year, the cement shortage is projected at 26 million 40 kg bags, with supply at 308 million bags versus a demand of 334 million bags.
In 1997, the shortage is at 5.2 million bags, with production at 401.8 million bags and demand at 407 million bags.
In 1998, the shortfall is 42.5 million bags, with supply at 454.5 million bags and usage at 497 million bags.

But in 1999, the situation will reverse to a surplus of 129.70 million bags with the expansion of existing cement plants and the opening of new ones. Supply is seen at 737.7 million bags compared with a demand forecast of 608 million bags.
